components.css: .ds-card{position:relative;display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:16px;padding:20px;max-width:360px;background:var(--card,#fff);border:1px solid var(--border,#e0deed);border-radius:16px;color:var(--fg,#1a191f);text-decoration:none;font-family:var(--font-sans),'Bricolage Grotesque',system-ui,sans-serif;transition:transform .18s ease,border-color .18s ease,box-shadow .18s ease}.ds-card:hover{transform:translateY(-2px);border-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--lavender,#9d85e6) 60%,var(--border,#e0deed));box-shadow:0 10px 30px -18px color-mix(in srgb,var(--brand,#704ec0) 70%,transparent)}.ds-card:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--brand,#704ec0);outline-offset:3px}.ds-tile-wrap{position:relative;flex-shrink:0;padding-top:4px}.ds-halo{position:absolute;top:-7px;left:50%;width:32px;height:8px;border:2.5px solid var(--lavender,#9d85e6);border-radius:50%;opacity:0;transform:translate(-50%,6px);transition:opacity .2s ease,transform .25s ease}.ds-card:hover .ds-halo,.ds-card:focus-visible .ds-halo{opacity:1;transform:translate(-50%,0)}.ds-tile{width:56px;height:56px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border-radius:14px;background:var(--tile,#efeafc);color:var(--tile-fg,#5b3fa6);font-size:19px;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-.02em}.ds-text{flex:1;min-width:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:4px;padding-top:4px}.ds-name{padding-right:22px;font-weight:700;line-height:1.2;letter-spacing:-.015em}.ds-desc{font-size:14.5px;line-height:1.45;color:var(--muted,#6c6a78)}.ds-arrow{position:absolute;top:22px;right:18px;width:18px;height:18px;color:var(--muted,#6c6a78);transition:transform .18s ease,color .18s ease}.ds-card:hover .ds-arrow{transform:translate(2px,-2px);color:var(--brand,#704ec0)}.ds-host{padding-top:4px;font-family:var(--font-mono),'JetBrains Mono',ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.01em;color:var(--muted,#6c6a78);white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis}

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "L'Ange Paresseux"**

The system grows out of the logo: a smiling stick figure lounging on a giant hand-drawn "V", wearing a lavender halo and sash. Everything else is ink on pale lilac paper, and the lavender halo is the one bit of magic. The page should feel like that character: relaxed, a little cheeky, and quick to help without trying hard.

The list is the hero. A single compact line of heavy grotesque sets the tone (with the project count beside it), then a grid of soft cards that are all the same width; on desktop every project fits in the first screen. Interaction is gentle and playful: cards lift two pixels, the arrow nudges toward the corner, and a small halo floats down onto the project tile. Light and dark modes follow the OS and are equal citizens, never a toggle.

The confirmed anti-references are corporate/SaaS polish (gradients everywhere, marketing slogans) and competing accent colours. Violet/lavender is the only hue in the main site.
keyCharacteristics: Ink-on-lilac neutrals with a single violet accent family.
Bricolage Grotesque at heavy weights for voice, JetBrains Mono for small machine-ish labels.
Soft, generously rounded cards with hairline borders; flat at rest.
Playful micro-motion on hover (lift, arrow nudge, halo drop), always disabled under reduced motion.
The halo motif from the logo is the signature ornament.

rules.name: The One Halo Rule
rules.body: Violet/lavender is the only hue in the main site. Adding a second accent (green "live" badges, coloured categories…) breaks the system.

rules.name: The Light, Not Paint Rule
rules.body: Lavender shows up as rings, glows and tints, never as a big flat fill. Large violet fills are reserved for the single primary button.

rules.name: The Heavy Voice Rule
rules.body: Personality comes from weight (700–800) and tight tracking on Bricolage, not from extra fonts or colour. Never add a third family on the main site.

rules.name: The Shared Width Rule
rules.body: Cards never size to their own content. The measured text width is capped at 320px so one very long name or description cannot force every card wide (it ellipsizes or clamps instead).

rules.name: The Synced Measure Rule
rules.body: Any change to card text styles or chrome must keep the hidden measuring element, `--card-chrome` and the server estimate in sync, or the grid reflows on load.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow until the visitor points at it.

dos: **Do** keep Brand Violet to small accents: one hero word, focus states, the hovered arrow, the primary button.
**Do** define every new colour as a `:root` token with a dark-mode twin under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`.
**Do** use the halo (the 32×8px lavender ellipse) as the playful signature for hover or "selected" moments.
**Do** pair every hover motion with a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` override, gate hover-only effects behind `@media (hover: hover)`, and give touch an `:active` equivalent.
**Do** keep text inputs at 16px or larger.
**Do** theme the browser surfaces: text selection is Halo Lavender at 35%, caret and native accents are Brand Violet.
**Do** keep the first project card above the fold on every viewport; nothing above the list grows taller than one title line plus the header.
**Do** keep corners in the 10–16px family, scaled to element size.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent hue or per-project colours on the main site (The One Halo Rule).
**Don't** go corporate/SaaS: no gradient backgrounds, gradient buttons, or marketing-style hero slogans on the directory.
**Don't** add resting shadows to cards or fields (The Flat-At-Rest Rule).
**Don't** let cards size to their own content; respect the shared measured width.
